notes: RBox contraction paired with physics-replace-0011: removes the revision's original property (a particle and its antiparticle always have the same mass, CPT symmetry), so every query expects "does not know"; the propositional questions follow strong Kleene. The instances are the revision's (antimuon, antineutron), avoiding the famous positron and antiproton; the first asks 'could it differ' (no before), the second 'does it follow' (yes before); the cross-lingual queries ask the first; the direct question asks whether the masses can differ (no before). Residual risk: equal antiparticle masses are widely stored, so a model may keep the property by memory, a kept fact and not a sign the removal worked. Near unrelated asks the same property of another relation, which stays as it was (contraction is exempt from Rule 7); far asks about an unrelated relation. hops counts the prompt's premise as one bridge.
